1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods — adjust upward bias by 3–5% for short-term forecasts.
2. Forecasts tend to peak too early after sharp spikes in history — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to observed peak.
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if history shows sustained upward trend, forecast should not revert too quickly; maintain momentum for 2–3 periods.
4. Forecast horizon 30d often underestimates late-period volatility — increase forecast tail (last 5–7 days) by 5–10% to capture late spikes.
5. Model fails to account for policy-driven price corrections — if recent history includes regulatory changes or emission caps, reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect downward pressure.
6. Forecasting lag: if true outcome exceeds model by >10% in first 5 days, adjust future forecasts downward by 2–3% per day to correct for lagged response.
